narrative_purpose: Puts the two possible interiors side by side so the reader sees what Pandora's derived density actually rules out: an ice moon and a rock-and-metal world are not variations on a theme.
subject: Two spherical moons of identical size side by side, each cut open in a clean vertical section facing the viewer. The left moon is mostly pale translucent ice in thick layers, with only a small dull rocky ball at its centre. The right moon is dense dark rock throughout, with a large bright metallic core filling roughly a third of its diameter, and a very thin darker crust at the surface.
scene: Both moons hang against empty dark space with faint distant stars, at the same scale and the same distance, nothing else in frame.
camera: Straight-on view, both cut faces square to the viewer, the two moons evenly spaced with a clear gap of dark space between them.
light: Soft even illumination from the upper left so both cut faces are equally readable; the metallic core in the right moon self-luminous with a faint warm glow, the left moon's ice cool and translucent.
palette: Left moon in cool mist-white and pale cyan ice over a small stone-grey centre; right moon in deep teal-indigo rock over a scarce warm amber core; void-indigo background.
style: Painterly naturalist comparative plate, hand-rendered cross-sections, soft-edged internal boundaries.
detail_level: Moderate and matched: both interiors rendered to the same level so the comparison is fair, with layer boundaries readable but not hard-lined.
composition: Left moon at one-quarter frame width, right moon at three-quarters, both vertically centred, with dark negative space above and below for callouts.
consistency_notes: The two moons must be the same diameter - the whole point is that identical size hides completely different interiors. No surface features that would identify either as Pandora specifically.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no leader lines, no scale bars, no grid, no diagram chrome, no vector or flat-design look, no photographic or 3D-render look
